body.title: Write the triage protocol for a single veto
body.body:
## What is delivered
A written triage protocol for a single veto whose grounds bring information beyond the scope considered before the decision.

Cover at least: how the facts claimed are verified (records, sensors, independent sources, people and local Dks of the context); how the meaning of the new information for this decision is established, not only its truth; how error, misunderstanding and manipulation are detected, including coordinated vetoes with copied grounds; how the smallest adjustment is chosen (exception, bounded test) before any general change; time limits so that verification does not make the veto useless; how the anonymity of whoever vetoed is protected when the grounds could identify them; and how a contested triage reaches the independent member panel. Include one worked case.

## Why it is needed
A single well-founded veto can change a decision. That is what makes the veto intelligent, and it is also what makes it an attack surface. The safeguards exist in prose across UID, Dk and the governance; nothing yet says step by step how a triage is carried out and recorded.

## Where to start
The veto chain in [UID](https://uid.drayker.org), the council and panel description in this repository, and the constitutional alignment paper in [Dknowledge](https://dknowledge.drayker.org).

---
This is an open function: small enough for one person to finish, defined enough that the result composes with the rest. Claim it in this thread before starting so two people do not carry the same function, and deliver through a pull request to `master`. It appears on the board at https://drayker.org/#org/fn

body.title: Write how a council works
body.body:
## What is delivered
A first version of "how a council works": how a council is formed, how someone joins one, which councils exist or should exist, how a council records a position, and what weight that position carries in DFMP.

## Why it is needed
DFMP says validation runs alongside development and that papers pass through the DAOs and/or councils depending on their purpose. Nothing about the councils themselves is published. For a system whose legitimacy rests on decentralized peer review, that is a load-bearing absence.

## Where to start
The DFMP README and `dfmpp/README.md` describe where councils appear in the process. This function fills in what happens inside them.

You do not need authority to write this — propose it, and let the communities argue it through.
## Prior material

Drayker has earlier work on this subject in its own knowledge base — drafts, mostly in Portuguese, written before the public repositories took their current shape. It is not published yet. If you take this function, say so in the thread and the relevant material will be published alongside it, so you are consolidating and arguing with existing thinking rather than starting from a blank page.

---
This is an open function: small enough for one person to finish, defined enough that the result composes with the rest. Claim it in this thread before starting so two people do not carry the same function, and deliver through a pull request to `master`. It appears on the board at https://drayker.org/#org/fn

body.title: Member councils formed for each question replace the judicial panel
body.body_html:
Aligns this repository with the decisions of October 2026:

  • member councils formed for each question instead of an independent judicial panel chosen by lot;
  • no forks or open-code claims for Dk: auditable through Dknowledge and DFM by permission level, with divergence tested in parallel;
  • Dk Global decides only inside the space the constitution gives it, open to representation, proposals and justified vetoes;
  • units of account instead of a token economy.

🤖 Generated with Claude Code

body.title: Councils and judicial panel: sortition, veto chain, triage of contested vetoes
body.body:
Alignment pass across the `draykerdk` organization, on the branch `alinhamento/2026-09` in every affected repository.

## Changes

- docs: judicial panel as in ch. 51 of the book (2.7.1): drawn by lot from the membership
- docs: the panel reads and writes the veto chain; unify footer
- docs: the panel hears contested triages; the situated veto is justified
- docs: remove book citations

## Across the organization

- Governance corrected: PAP is Projects & Applications, DFMP is the DFM proposal process, the founding account is `Hyadhuad`, and the governance horizon runs from the founding Embassy through the DAF into PAP.
- The veto chain specified in UID: signed, hash-linked vetoes that carry their real grounds even when anonymous; vetoes weighed by grounds, not counted; one veto with grounds beyond the decision's scope can lead to an adjustment after advanced triage.
- Direction states 2033 as the objective, measured by what works rather than by the date.
- Intelligence is a partner, never the master.
- English is the canonical documentation language.
- Documentation states its own claims and does not cite outside books as authority.

Documentation only. Nothing here claims an implemented system.

Supersedes #2, closed when the branch was renamed.
